definitions.explanation: A grammatical category that locates an event in time, marking past, present, or future. A core term in linguistics and language teaching.

examples.japanese: {動詞|どうし}の{時制|じせい}を{覚|おぼ}える。
{英語|えいご}は{日本語|にほんご}より{時制|じせい}が{複雑|ふくざつ}だ。
examples.english: English has more complex tenses than Japanese.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}には{未来|みらい}{時制|じせい}が{独立|どくりつ}してなく、{現在形|げんざいけい}で{未来|みらい}を{表|あらわ}すことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Japanese doesn't have an independent future tense; the future is often expressed with the present form.

notes:
Compound of {時|じ} (time) + {制|せい} (system). A specialized linguistic term, used mainly in grammar instruction and academic linguistics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {現在|げんざい}{時制|じせい}: present tense
- {過去|かこ}{時制|じせい}: past tense
- {未来|みらい}{時制|じせい}: future tense
- {時制|じせい}の{一致|いっち}: tense agreement (sequence of tenses)
- {時制|じせい}を{変|か}える: to change the tense

SIMILAR WORDS:
- テンス: tense — the loanword equivalent, used in linguistics papers
- {相|そう}: aspect — a related grammatical category (e.g., progressive, perfective)
- {法|ほう}: mood — another verbal category (indicative, imperative, etc.)
